title: Michael Forest Dies: Actor In Roger Corman B-Movies, ‘Star Trek’s Apollo Was 97
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Suspends Val Chmerkovskiy For TikTok Referencing Will Smith Oscar Moment; Dancer Responds, “Instinct Was To Defend My Wife” Miley Cyrus Tearfully Remembers Dolly Parton At Hollywood Bowl Concert, Performs ‘Jolene’ Harry Styles Pays Tribute To Liam Payne With New Song At Madison Square Garden Concert View All October 17, 2026 6:42am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Michael Forest in 'Ski Troop Attack' (1960) Getty Michael Forest , a prolific and longtime character actor who appeared in the B movies of Roger Corman, lent his voice to numerous anime projects and guest starred in scores of TV series from The Adventures of Rin Tin Tin, The Twilight Zone and The Dick Van Dyke Show to Silk Stalkings, daytime soaps and a memorably outsized role on Star Trek , died October 14. He was 97. Sparks most recently resided at an assisted living facility in Sparks, Nevada. His death was announced on Facebook by his friend James A. Brown. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries Obituaries Bernie Orenstein Dies: Writer-Producer On ‘Sanford & Son,’ ‘That Girl,’ ‘Kate & Allie’ & More Was 95 Among the actor’s numerous TV roles was a favorite among Star Trek fans: Forest played the giant Greek god Apollo in the memorable 1967 episode “Who Mourns for Adonais?” Watch on Deadline Other notable TV roles include a former boyfriend of The Dick Van Dyke Show ‘s Laura Petrie (Mary Tyler Moore) who gets set up for a date with Rose Marie’s ever-single Sally Rogers (Laura doesn’t know he has become a priest. That same year – 1964 – Forest played a member of an alien biker gangs in The Twilight Zone episode “Black Leather Jackets.” Just a sampling of his many other TV credits in the 1950s, ’60s and ’70s includes appearances on episodes of Z orro, Have Gun – Will Travel, Maverick, Ben Casey, The Outer Limits, Gunsmoke, Gomer Pyle: USMC, I Spy, Mission: Impossible, Gilligan’s Island, Get Smart, The Rookies and Who’s The Boss. Forest also was a busy voice and dubbing actor, appearing in hundreds of animated films lending his skills to hundreds of The 1990s and 2000s saw Forest largely pivoting to voice work and dubbing for animated series and video games including entries in the Power Rangers and Dynasty Warriors franchises, World of Warcraft and various anime projects. Michael Forest as Apollo in 1967 Star Trek episode ‘Who Mourns for Adonais?’ On the big screen, Forest appeared in such drive-in notables as 1959’s Beast From Haunted Cave and Roger Corman’s The Saga of the Viking Women and Their Voyage to the Waters of the Great Sea Serpent (1958), Ski Troop Attack (1960) and sword-and-sandal adventure Atlas (1961). Decades later he played a pilot in the Tom Hanks 2000 film Cast Away, among other late career appearances. Over the years he appeared in the soaps As The World Turns, Days of Our Lives and The Young and the Restless. In 2013, Forest reprised his Apollo role for the fan-made web series Star Trek Continues . Born Gerald Michael Charlebois on April 17, 1929, in Harvey, North Dakota, Forest moved to Los Angeles in 1955 and met director Corman through an acting class, leading to their collaborations that began in the late 1950s. Forest was preceded in death by his wife, the actress Diana Hale, who passed away in 2022. full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Street Fighter’ Socks $31M, ‘You Can See Everything’ Has Lines Around The Block With $12M+ Docu Milestone – Saturday Update Chase Infiniti-Starring ‘The Julia Set’ Acquired By Sony Pictures Classics After TIFF Premiere Indie Film Studio Bleecker Street Bought By Outerlight Entertainment View All October 17, 2026 8:01am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Street Fighter' and 'You Can See Everything' Paramount/A24 SATURDAY AM: It’s a healthy third weekend at the October box office even with a bellyflop in 20th Century Studio’s $60M Whalefall in the mix which is only swallowing a $7.5M opening. Paramount/Legendary/Capcom’s Street Fighter is doing what it’s supposed to do with a $31M start, largely pulling in an older dude demo over 35 at 45% (that’s what’s walloping Whalefall ‘s business, the overlap in male demos). But the scene stealer again this year after Backrooms (and even Primetime ) is A24 with their 3 hour Elizabeth Holmes non-fiction title You Can See Everything which is charting the second best opening ever for a documentary at the box office with $12M-$14M at 855 screens, right behind 2004’s Fahrenheit 9/11 ($23.9M). Eight years after the tech blood analysis company Theranos cratered due to controversy, and four years after Hulu’s Emmy winning Amanda Seyfried starring limited series, The Dropout, who knew there was still this much interest in Holmes? Well, A24, you certainly seduced everyone with your sneaky secret world premiere mic drop at Telluride. We’re getting reports about 1,300 sellouts so far this weekend and lines around the block for You Can See Everything at the Village East in NYC as well as the Belcourt in Nashville, Tenn. See below: Watch on Deadline View this post on Instagram There is no CinemaScore on You Can See Everything because it’s under 1,000 screens. Definite recommend is an unprecedented on Screen Engine/Rentrak’s PostTrak with 91% for a documentary — that’s the type of scores successful Marvel movies like Black Panther would put up back in the day. Typically, A24 movies succeed in dividing. Not this one. The Gen Zers are gobbling this up with 18-34 showing up at 62%. Overall positive score on Screen Engine/Rentrak’s PostTrak is 98% so A24 can take that to the bank. 56% to 44% male-female turnout with moviegoers making it a date night (44% came with a spouse, partner, BF or GF). Big walk-up business with 41% purchasing their tickets the day of. Diversity demos are Caucasian at 68%, Latino and Hispanic at 15%, Asian American at 8% and Black at 5%. Top grossing theaters yesterday for You Can See Everything were the AMC Empire, followed by the AMC Kabuki in San Francisco, and then AMC Lincoln Square. New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Chicago, Boston and Seattle are the top moneymaking cities for the Lance Oppenheim and Fielder directed documentary. RelishMix beams, “ You Can See Everything has a very selective platform roll-out with only an Instagram at 13K fans and 42M views on YouTube off of two videos dropped by A24. Share-reposting stats run at 61:1 which is exceptional. Overall, awareness stats of 102M for You Can See Everything , next to indie-dramas, are outpacing by 40%.” This is also boosted by co-director and the documentary’s deadpan star Nathan Fielder, whose Instagram has hit 1M fans, and which has also fed 30M video views. On Thursday, the actress shared a statement explaining that she “never took a day of [the show] for granted” after series co-creator Lorre wrote in his new memoir Sitcom that he “was, in fact, correct” about his initial reluctance to cast her as Christy Plunkett in the sitcom.
